name: UNDER PROSPERITY
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE DARK
LOOK_AT: Dark with a texture to it. The lamp makes a room the size of the lamp, and the rest of the underworld waits its turn.
I turned the lamp down once, to see what the dark was like on its own. I turned it back up.
It is not empty. It is only unlit.
LISTEN_TO: My own ears, ringing faintly. Underground, silence has a pitch. I could tune to it.
The ringing in my ears, settling on a note. A little flat. Of course it is.
My own heartbeat, which I have not heard in some years, keeping better time than the town.

subjects.name: THE AIR
LOOK_AT: You cannot see it, and down here that is the most interesting thing about it: the flame leans. The air is going somewhere.
Nothing to look at. There has never been anything to look at.
There is nothing to see. I keep looking anyway, like a man rereading a letter he knows by heart.
LISTEN_TO: Moving. Warmer than the day. I have heard this before, at the top of a hole, and used it to evict a raccoon.
Warmer. It has been warmer every foot.
Moving, and warmer. I have stopped being surprised by it and started paying attention.

subjects.name: THE WALLS
LOOK_AT: Clay, then rock, then a seam of something the lamp takes an interest in. I am declining to be excited. The territory has trained me thoroughly.
Rock.
Rock, mostly.
LISTEN_TO: Water, somewhere inside the stone, going about its business.
Water inside the stone again, going about its business.
Nothing I can name yet. I am listening anyway. It is what I am for.

subjects.name: THE TIMBERING
LOOK_AT: Old timbering, not mine, not recent. Someone was down here before the town was up there, and shored it like they meant to come back.
The joints are pegged, not nailed, by somebody who had more time than nails.
It has held a town on top of it for twelve years without a word of complaint. I know men who could learn from it.
LISTEN_TO: The wood takes the mountain's weight and says so, once in a while, quietly.
A long creak overhead, and then the mountain settles back.
Nothing for a while. Then one small tick, like a clock deciding not to strike.

overrides.PULL: The timber holds the mountain. I hold my curiosity. Everyone keeps their post.

subjects.name: THE SEAM
LOOK_AT: The seam, where the lamp stops being casual. I have seen color in a pan, in a bottle, on a scale. I have never seen it at home before. It is different at home.
It runs at a slant into the dark, wider than my hand and further than the lamp.
I have looked at it for a long time. It does not do anything. It does not need to.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. It has been keeping this quiet for longer than there have been ears.
Nothing. Gold has never had to raise its voice.
Nothing. Twelve years of a town, built on top of a silence.

overrides.PICK_UP: Not with my hands. This one goes through the window, into the book, past Winnie's scales — the whole liturgy. Some gold you take; this gold I intend to file.

subjects.name: THE OLD LANTERN
LOOK_AT: A lantern, not mine, hung on a spike and burned dry — years dry. Its glass is clean. Someone tended it, once, regularly.
The wick has been trimmed square, the way a careful man trims one.
It hangs where it would light the way back up, not the way in. Whoever kept it always meant to leave.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Long finished. But kept, not abandoned. There is a difference and you can hear it.
Nothing. Its tin cooled a long time ago.
Nothing. It is waiting for its keeper, and its keeper is not coming down tonight.

overrides.USE: Not mine to light. Its keeper knows where it hangs, and I find I want him to find it as he left it.

subjects.name: THE FOOTPRINTS
LOOK_AT: Boot prints in the clay, preserved like the creek bank's, but one pair, many visits, all the same stride. Even. He was counting.
The stride never shortens, coming or going. Whoever made these was never in a hurry and never tired.
Mine cross his now, clumsier and in a hurry. He would not have approved.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. But the silence here is worn smooth, like a path.
Nothing. The clay has kept every step and repeats none of them.
Nothing. A path nobody walks any more makes exactly this sound.

subjects.name: THE WAY BACK UP
LOOK_AT: The rope to the surface, and the coin of gray light at the top of it. Up there this is still the worthless claim. I am in no hurry to correct anyone.
Daylight, a long way up, the size of a coin.
The coin of light has moved. It is later up there than I thought.
LISTEN_TO: The surface, at a great distance: wind, and the suggestion of a town.
The town. Very faint. Somebody is arguing about a boundary.
Somebody up there laughing, very far off. They do not know yet.

overrides.TALK_TO: I called up that I was all right. The gray coin of daylight did not answer, which is how daylight is.

subjects.name: THE TUNNEL
LOOK_AT: Forty feet of my own digging. It is not square and it is not swept and Nickel Pratt would weep.
There is a bend in it where I lost my nerve and a straight stretch after where I found it again.
My pick marks are everywhere and none of them in a line. It is the most honest piece of work I have ever done.
LISTEN_TO: Air. Still moving. Still going somewhere.
My own breathing, loud in here. The tunnel keeps nothing to itself.
A trickle of loose dirt from the roof, then quiet: the tunnel, settling into being a tunnel.

subjects.name: THE ROCK FACE
LOOK_AT: Rock.
Rock. I have looked at it enough to know it is rock.
Still rock.
LISTEN_TO: …Different. Not by much.
The same small difference. It has not gone away.
Not much. Not nothing.

subjects.name: THE LAMP
LOOK_AT: One lamp, and about four hours of oil in it.
Three hours of oil now. I am doing the arithmetic more often than I would like.
It throws my shadow up the wall, three times my size and twice as confident.
LISTEN_TO: Burning.
A soft hiss as the wick drinks.
Burning, still. The most reassuring word in the language.

subjects.name: THE TUNING FORK
LOOK_AT: My father thought this was a sensible investment. He was, on the evidence, the only person in my family who has ever been right about anything.
The tines are worn bright at the ends, where I have struck it on ten thousand boot heels.
It is the only thing I own that is exactly what it claims to be.
LISTEN_TO: A. Four hundred and forty. It is still the only correct thing within a hundred miles.
I struck it. A, held, ringing down to nothing.
A. The same A it gave in my father's shop. Some things do not move.

subjects.name: THE FLOOR
LOOK_AT: Clay, packed hard by somebody's boots long before mine.
My own prints, and the drag marks of my pick behind them.
It is level, more or less, which down here counts as hospitality.
LISTEN_TO: My boots, thudding, close and flat.
Grit under my heel, very loud in all this quiet.
Nothing, when I stand still. I stand still a while longer, just to hear it.
